what: The score is the fixed cheapest-insertion delta minus the best improving 2-opt gain obtainable by breaking an edge incident to the candidate, minus a modest demand-weighted depot-distance credit. It scans only the current route, uses the supplied distance matrix, and costs O(len(route)) time with O(1) extra space.
why: Subtracting a candidate-touching 2-opt gain aligns construction with the stated post-construction local search without performing a forbidden quadratic 2-opt scan. The radial credit follows generalized insertion logic: remote customers are expensive to leave as future route seeds, while the demand adjustment mildly favors customers that may become difficult to fit later. The method remains local: its predicted 2-opt move can disappear after later insertions, it does not model complete capacity packing or other routes, and the fixed weights are design choices requiring held-out validation rather than claimed empirical improvements.
